items.stem: A fault-tolerant batch job can be interrupted and resumed. Which EC2 purchasing option minimizes its cost?

options.rationale: Correct: Spot offers the deepest discount for interruption-tolerant workloads.
On-Demand costs more and is unnecessary for an interruptible job.
Reservations suit steady long-running load, not a one-off batch job.
Dedicated Hosts add cost for isolation the job does not need.

items.explanation: Correct: Spot Instances are cheapest for interruption-tolerant workloads.

items.stem: Which TWO improve the security of an EC2 instance? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Restrict the SSH security-group rule to known source IP ranges
options.rationale: Correct: limiting source ranges reduces exposure.

options.text: Attach an IAM role instead of storing static access keys on the instance
options.rationale: Correct: instance roles supply temporary credentials with no static keys.

options.text: Open all ports to 0.0.0.0/0 so nothing is blocked
options.rationale: Opening all ports widely exposes the instance.

options.text: Embed long-lived access keys in the AMI
options.rationale: Baking keys into an AMI is a serious credential-leak risk.

items.explanation: Correct: scoping SSH rules and using an IAM role both strengthen instance security.

items.stem: You need capacity to recover automatically if an instance fails and to scale with demand. What should you use?

options.text: An Auto Scaling group with a launch template and health checks
options.rationale: Correct: an ASG replaces unhealthy instances and scales to demand.
A standalone instance has no self-healing or scaling.
S3 stores objects and does not run compute.

options.text: A manually launched fleet with no group
options.rationale: Unmanaged instances do not auto-heal or scale.

items.explanation: Correct: an Auto Scaling group provides self-healing and demand-based scaling.
